name: Praise the Sun, Fire the Gun
description:
{"ops":[{"insert":"Praise the Sun, Fire the Gun"},{"attributes":{"header":1},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"This Heliod Commander deck is a highly optimized blend of control, stax pressure, and a consistent Ballista-based win condition  "},{"attributes":{"color":"#e8e8e8","background":"#22242a"},"insert":"© Marsitz"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
At first glance, Heliod looks like a lifegain commander. A friendly god handing out counters and blessings. "},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"That's a lie."},{"insert":"
This deck isn't interested in gaining life. It isn't interested in combat. It isn't interested in fair Magic.
This is a mono-white control deck disguised as a devotion commander.

The goal is simple: slow the table to a crawl, force everyone to play by your rules, and quietly assemble one of the most compact kill conditions in the format. 
While opponents argue with Rule of Law effects, search restrictions, graveyard hate, and a growing pile of "you can't do that" permanents, Heliod patiently waits for the moment when a Ballista or Triskelion enters the battlefield and ends the discussion entirely.

General Strategy"},{"attributes":{"header":2},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
The deck operates on a simple principle:
"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"If everyone is playing one spell per turn, I'd like to be the player whose one spell matters most."},{"insert":"
Most tables are built around velocity. Multiple spells. Explosive turns. Giant stack battles. This deck attacks the foundation itself. Rule of Law. Deafening Silence. Archon of Emeria. Eidolon of Rhetoric.
While opponents are forced to navigate a maze of restrictions, Heliod develops incrementally. A mana rock here. A tutor there. A protection spell held patiently in hand.
The deck rarely wins quickly.
Instead, it creates a game state where everyone else slowly realizes they're no longer playing the game they sat down for.

You Shouldn't Play This Deck If..."},{"attributes":{"header":2},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"You enjoy explosive turns."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"You like drawing half your deck."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"You want every game to end quickly."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"You enjoy making friends at the table."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"You feel guilty when three opponents collectively sigh."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
You SHOULD Play This Deck If..."},{"attributes":{"header":2},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"You enjoy being the sheriff at a lawless table."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"You love saying "No" without technically countering anything."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"You appreciate winning through positioning rather than raw card advantage."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"You enjoy making opponents solve impossible puzzles."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"You believe silence is a valid win condition."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
MVP Cards"},{"attributes":{"header":2},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
Ranger-Captain of Eos"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"One of the strongest cards in the deck.
It tutors combo pieces, finds utility creatures, protects winning turns, and occasionally functions as a one-sided Time Walk when sacrificed at the right moment.

Grand Abolisher"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"The closest thing mono-white has to declaring martial law.
When this card resolves, opponents suddenly discover how many interaction spells they've been saving.

Rule of Law Effects"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"The true engine of the deck.
Many players view these cards as support pieces.
They're not.
They're the strategy.

The One Ring"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"An absurd source of card advantage that helps mono-white keep pace in games that drag far longer than opponents expected.

Walking Ballista"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"The gun.
The entire deck is built around creating a game state where this card becomes inevitable.


Win Conditions"},{"attributes":{"header":2},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
Heliod + Walking Ballista"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"The classic.
Give Ballista lifelink.
Remove a counter.
Deal damage.
Gain life.
Heliod replaces the counter.
Repeat until nobody remains.
Simple. Efficient. Beautiful.

Heliod + Triskelion"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"A slightly clunkier backup plan that wins through the exact same principle.
The table usually knows what's coming.
That rarely helps them.

Concession"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"A surprisingly common outcome.
Sometimes opponents look around at Rule of Law, Drannith Magistrate, Rest in Peace, Aven Mindcensor, and a hand full of dead cards and decide they've suffered enough.


Coolest Plays"},{"attributes":{"header":2},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
Casting Silence during upkeep and watching three players collectively realize they no longer have a turn."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Flashing in a stax piece with Liberator at exactly the wrong moment for someone else."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Using Ranger-Captain to tutor a combo piece and then sacrificing him the following turn to force it through."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Winning through a stack containing exactly zero counterspells because nobody was allowed to cast any."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Looking completely harmless until Heliod suddenly turns a Ballista into a machine gun."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
Weak Points & What To Watch For"},{"attributes":{"header":2},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
Card Advantage"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"The deck is efficient, not explosive.
If the game becomes a grind and The One Ring doesn't show up, resource management matters.

Creature Removal"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Heliod is remarkably resilient, but combo creatures are not.
Protecting the actual kill piece is often more important than protecting your commander.

Being the Archenemy"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"People remember Rule of Law.
People remember Drannith Magistrate.
People definitely remember the player responsible for both.
Accept that attention is part of the strategy.
Patience"},{"attributes":{"header":3},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"This deck rewards restraint.
Many games are won because you waited one turn longer than everyone expected.

One Final Note"},{"attributes":{"header":2},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
Heliod isn't a prison deck.
Prison implies permanence.
This deck is a negotiation.
You are simply presenting the table with a choice:
Play fair, play slow, and maybe survive.
Or let the sun rise, and hear the Ballista fire.
"}]}
